priceSnapshot.note: SCHEDULING DISCLOSURE FIRST, because it changes how this report should be read. This is the MORNING session and it ran at 21:10 COT, roughly fourteen hours after its 06:50 slot. The scheduler did not fire on time. Everything in here is stamped with the real clock, not the nominal one, and the comparison window against the 08:15 COT midnight report is thirteen hours rather than the usual five. Now the tape. Price at 77,708.5 is DOWN 972.2 points, 1.24 percent, from the 78,680.7 the midnight session recorded, and the path there is the whole story. The 78,830.0 ADD gate that midnight wrote FIRED cleanly - the 1H bar opening 2026-08-30T16:00Z closed 79,307.7, a full 477.7 points through the line - and price extended to 79,387.8. Then it reversed the entire move and more, running 2,471.2 points down to 76,916.6 on the 23:45Z 15m bar, which is 69.3 points above the 76,847.3 Warsh flush low that has been the invalidation level all week. That low held. Price has since bounced to 78,160.0 and settled back into the 77,500-to-77,900 band. Two gates therefore resolved in opposite directions inside one session, and the reduce gate is the one that stuck.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $77,400.0 AND a failure to reclaim it on either of the next two hourly bars. This level is not drawn from a chart pattern - it is the lower edge of the second-largest MEASURED long-liquidation cluster of the last hour, the 77,400-to-77,500 band that absorbed 764,091 USD of forced long selling on OKX alone. Losing it re-opens the 77,000-to-77,100 pocket where 1,048,285 USD of longs were already flushed, and beneath that sits the 76,847.3 invalidation. At 308.5 points below spot the gate is 0.70 hourly ATRs away - slightly outside the 0.4-to-0.6 band this log usually works in, but the band gave 176 to 265 points and there is no structure in that range, only air between the current chop and the liquidation shelf. Structure wins over the band when the two disagree and the structure is measured rather than inferred.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $78,180.0, which clears the 78,160.0 bounce high printed on the 00:30Z 15m bar by 20 points. That is 471.5 points above spot, 1.07 hourly ATRs, and deliberately far. The reason is that 78,080.0 - the base the midnight breakout was built on - has now been lost on three consecutive settled hourly closes, so it has flipped from support to resistance and a marginal poke back above it proves nothing. Only a close through the bounce high says the flush was a liquidity grab rather than the start of a trend leg, and it would also clear the 78,047-to-78,132 pocket where the only meaningful short liquidations of the session sit.

decisionBox.changed: Bias flips from midnight's BULLISH to RANGE with a BEARISH tilt, and the box from ADD to REDUCE. Four things drove it, in order of weight. FIRST, midnight's own 78,080.0 reduce gate fired and CONFIRMED - the 1H bar opening 2026-08-30T23:00Z settled at 77,640.2, and both of the next two hourly bars failed to reclaim the line, closing 77,901.5 and then 77,605.8. That is the cleanest full confirmation of a reduce gate in this log. SECOND, the 28 August US spot-ETF print finally became readable and it is an OUTFLOW of 201.9m, which ENDS the nine-session inflow streak that was the single strongest bull argument in every report since 17 August. THIRD, real liquidation data was retrieved for the first time in this log, and it shows 2,604,844 USD of long liquidations against 278,485 USD of short liquidations in one hour - forced selling outweighing forced buying by 9.35 to one. FOURTH, midnight's ADD gate fired and failed: acting on it would have bought near 79,300 into a 1,599-point reversal. The stop reference drops to 76,800.0, just under the 76,847.3 invalidation, and is flagged RECOMMENDED because the next scheduled session is midnight, roughly five hours away, and the measured flow shows a market actively hunting stops.

liquidation.note: MEASURED, not estimated. This is the volume-weighted centre of the 77,000-to-77,100 bucket, which absorbed 1,048,285 USD of forced long selling on OKX between 00:26Z and 00:28Z on 31 August - the single largest cluster in the retrieved window and 40.2 percent of all long liquidations in it. Individual fills of 400, 158.19, 152.84 and 121.45 contracts printed inside a two-second span at 77,044.5, 77,029.1 and 77,065.8. Marked as the magnet because it is both the biggest pool and the level the market has already proven it will travel to. It sits 664.0 points below spot.

MEASURED. The 77,400-to-77,500 bucket took 764,091 USD of long liquidations, 29.3 percent of the window's total, including a 400-contract fill at 77,473.2 and a 200-contract fill at 77,431.0. This is the nearest genuine pool beneath the market at 258.5 points below spot, and it is why the reduce gate is set at 77,400.0 rather than somewhere prettier.

MEASURED. The 77,100-to-77,200 bucket took 346,610 USD, with a 154.01-contract fill at 77,155.3 and 100.17 at 77,164.9. It bridges the 77,450 shelf and the 77,044.5 magnet, so a break of the reduce gate is unlikely to stop cleanly here.

MEASURED. The 78,000-to-78,100 bucket took 74,063 USD of forced SHORT covering during the bounce, including a 70-contract fill at 78,073.1. Note the asymmetry - this is the largest pool above the market and it is fourteen times smaller than the largest pool below it. There is very little trapped short interest to squeeze.

MEASURED. The 78,100-to-78,200 bucket took 71,493 USD of short liquidations, dominated by one 81.98-contract fill at 78,132.5 at the exact 78,160.0 bounce high. That single fill is most of the pocket, which is a hint that the bounce ran out of fuel precisely where the last trapped shorts were cleared.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is DOWN and this time the measurement says so rather than an inference from positioning. Forced long selling outweighed forced short covering 9.35 to one over the hour, and the pool structure is lopsided in the same direction: 2.16m USD of long liquidations sit in the three buckets below the market against 146k USD of short liquidations in the two buckets above it. One important caveat on how to read this. These are REALIZED fills, not resting orders - they mark where leverage HAS been cleared, not where it is still waiting. That makes them a good map of where stops were clustered and a decent proxy for where the next ones will sit, but it is not the forward heatmap a keyed CoinGlass feed would give. The honest reading is that the 77,000-to-77,500 corridor has already been swept once, which cuts both ways: the weak hands there are gone, but the market now knows the level is reachable.

etfFlows.note: THE STREAK IS OVER, and this is the most consequential new fact in the report. Farside's Bitcoin ETF flow table was reached live this session and the 28 August 2026 print - the number midnight called the single most important missing input and told this session to retrieve before anything else - is an OUTFLOW of 201.9m USD. It breaks a nine-session inflow run that ran 17 to 27 August and totalled 3,044.2m: 297.5, 189.3, 517.2, 606.3, 307.5, 337.6, 314.3, 232.2, 242.3. The composition of the outflow matters as much as the size. ARKB led at -114.9m, BITB -49.7m, IBIT -33.4m, HODL -13.2m, with only MSBT positive at +9.3m and FBTC flat. IBIT turning negative at all is notable given it supplied 2,296.2m of the streak's 3,044.2m. The print lands on the same session as the Warsh inflation message, so it reads as a genuine risk-off reaction rather than routine rebalancing, and it means the bid that carried price from 64,700 to 79,387 through late August stepped away before this weekend's reversal, not after it. streakDays is set to 0 rather than a negative count because one outflow day is not yet an outflow streak. Next print is Monday 31 August; there is no weekend ETF data.

liquidations.note: MEASURED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS LOG. The OKX /public/liquidation-orders feed returned 320 filled events covering 2026-08-31T00:10:12Z to 01:13:08Z, a 63-minute window that brackets the flush and the bounce. Long liquidations totalled 2,604,844 USD against 278,485 USD of shorts, so the skew field carries 9.35 - the ratio of forced long selling to forced short covering. NOTE THE CHANGE OF BASIS: previous reports put the OKX retail long/short ACCOUNT ratio in this field because no liquidation data was available. That ratio is still live and reads 1.14 at 2026-08-30T23:00Z, down from 1.21 at midnight and 1.16 at 28 August midday, so retail longs were partially flushed rather than adding into weakness. The 9.35 figure is the better number and future sessions should keep this basis. Three caveats, stated plainly. First, this is OKX only - it is a fraction of market-wide flow and the absolute USD figures are not comparable to an aggregated CoinGlass number. Second, the window is 63 minutes, not 24 hours. Third, these are realized fills, not resting orders. Open interest is 2,093,208,231.24 USD read at 2026-08-31T02:09:48Z, DOWN 6.98 percent from the 2,250,174,552.75 recorded at midnight - roughly 157m of notional has left the market while price fell 1.24 percent, which is textbook deleveraging rather than fresh shorting. Funding is 0.0000668854 per 8h, still positive so longs still pay, with the premium at -0.00053, meaning the perpetual trades under the index. Positive funding into a negative premium after a long flush is the signature of longs who have not fully capitulated.

calibration.rollingRecord: Nineteen sessions logged. The 0.4-to-0.6 ATR band tally now reads three clean confirmations, two whipsaws, one gate that whipsawed then confirmed on the second trigger, one gate that triggered twice and was voided both times, and - new this session - the first case where BOTH gates of a single box fired in the same window and pointed opposite ways, with the add failing and the reduce confirming.
calibration.note: Midnight wrote two gates and the tape hit both. The ADD gate at 78,830.0 fired first: the 1H bar opening 2026-08-30T16:00Z closed 79,307.7, some 477.7 points through the line, and price extended to a 79,387.8 high. It then reversed the entire move, and acting on that add would have bought near 79,300 into a 1,679-point drawdown to 76,916.6, leaving it 1,599 points underwater against the current 77,708.5. The ADD FAILED. The REDUCE gate at 78,080.0 fired second and CONFIRMED under its own rule: the 1H bar opening 23:00Z settled at 77,640.2, 439.8 points through the line, and both of the next two hourly bars failed to reclaim it, closing 77,901.5 and 77,605.8. Acting on that reduce would have sold near 78,080 against a current 77,708.5, so it saved 371.5 points and acting_helped is TRUE. Three findings worth carrying forward. FIRST, midnight set its reduce gate 600.7 points wide - 2.54 ATRs on the collapsed hourly ATR of 236.57 - and explicitly justified the width by arguing that a compressed ATR makes the 0.4-to-0.6 band too tight to be useful. That reasoning was correct and the wide gate worked; had it been placed at the band-implied 95-to-142 points it would have triggered during the ordinary afternoon chop hours before the real break. Widening a gate when ATR collapses is now a validated adjustment, not a one-off. SECOND, a compressed ATR is a warning about DIRECTION-FREE risk, not a bullish signal. Hourly ATR went from 236.57 to 441.23 in thirteen hours, an 86.5 percent expansion, and the release ran DOWN even though every EMA on every timeframe was aligned UP when the coil broke. The lesson is that an EMA stack in perfect bullish order told this desk nothing about which way a compressed range would resolve. THIRD, the strongest bear input was not technical and was not available at the time: the 28 August ETF outflow existed on Friday and simply had not been read. Midnight was right to name it the most important missing input, and a report that leans bullish on a nine-session inflow streak while unable to read the newest print of that streak is leaning on a number it does not have.
